hypothesis: Running best-of-N with the champion adapter and selecting the least-redundant set should push quality above the prior best, because redundancy is the remaining weak dimension and a whole-set binary redundancy count picks the verbatim candidate set that covers the most distinct information.
technique: Multiple candidate sets are generated with the champion adapter, then a deterministic Swift selector scores each whole verbatim set by a binary same-information redundancy count (fewer redundant pairs = better), with a greedy-output floor to break ties — no model call in the selection step.
result: Scored 0.388 on the full-30 gate (2 wins / 3 ties / 24 losses vs Sonnet); rubric showed atom=4, spec=4, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3 — redundancy did not improve meaningfully and coverage remained the binding constraint, falsifying the bet. Discarded.

stages.text: Over-produce N candidate sets via champion adapter
Pick least-redundant set by binary redundancy count
